seo.meta_title: '언제 밥 한번 먹어요' Isn't a Real Invitation | Korean Social Nuance
seo.meta_description: AI reads '언제 밥 한번 먹어요' as a dinner invitation. In Korea it's often a friendly goodbye. Learn how to tell — and how to make a real plan.

ai_failure.situation: Ending a chat with an acquaintance you ran into, who says '언제 밥 한번 먹어요!'
ai_failure.ai_mistake: Translates it as 'Let's have a meal sometime' and suggests replying with dates to set up the dinner.
ai_failure.why_it_fails: It's usually a warm way to say goodbye and keep the relationship open, like 'We should catch up sometime.' Pinning down a date right away can feel awkward unless the other person clearly means it.

natural_solution.rule: Return the warmth without forcing a schedule. A real plan comes with a concrete day, place or follow-up message.

alternatives.context: Friendly, natural reply that keeps it open
When you actually want to meet — propose a specific time
Warm goodbye toward someone older or more senior

nuance: Shared meals are central to Korean relationships, so offering one is a way of saying 'I value this connection.' Because the phrase carries goodwill rather than logistics, both sides understand it can stay hypothetical. The word 언제 (sometime) is the giveaway. If a Korean friend follows up later with a specific day, or the phrase becomes 이번 주에 밥 먹어요 (let's eat this week), it has turned into a real invitation.
